en menu.explanation: "En menu" means "a menu". To talk about the set meal a restaurant offers on one day, use "dagens menu" (the menu of the day): "Dagens menu er fisk" (The menu of the day is fish).

en mester.explanation: "En mester" means "a master / champion". To name a master of a craft, put the craft first: "en tømrermester" (a master carpenter).

en meter.explanation: "En meter" means "a meter". To say how tall something is, use a number before it: "Træet er ti meter højt" (The tree is ten meters tall).

en metode.explanation: "En metode" means "a method". To say you use a certain way of working, use "at bruge" (to use): "Jeg bruger en ny metode" (I use a new method).

en metro.explanation: "En metro" means "a metro". To say how you travel, use "med" (by): "Jeg kører med metroen" (I go by metro). Copenhagen has a metro.

en middag.explanation: "En middag" means "a dinner". When you give the time of day, "middag" also means "noon": "Klokken tolv er det middag" (At twelve o'clock it is noon). For the meal around that time, use "frokost" (lunch): "Vi spiser frokost klokken tolv" (We eat lunch at twelve).

en middagslur.explanation: "En middagslur" means "a nap". It is built from "middag" (midday) and "en lur" (a nap). To say you take a nap, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager en middagslur" (I take a nap).

en midtergang.explanation: "En midtergang" means "an aisle". It is built from "midt" (middle) and "en gang" (a hallway). The same "gang" is the word for a hallway in a house: "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

en migræne.explanation: "En migræne" means "a migraine". To name one attack, add "anfald" (attack): "et migræneanfald" (a migraine attack).

en mikrobølgeovn.explanation: "En mikrobølgeovn" means "a microwave oven". It is built from "mikro" (micro), "en bølge" (a wave) and "en ovn" (an oven). The shorter word is "en mikroovn" (a microwave): "Jeg varmer maden i mikroovnen" (I warm the food in the microwave).

en mikrofon.explanation: "En mikrofon" means "a microphone". To tell someone on a video call to unmute, say: "Slå din mikrofon til" (Turn on your microphone).

en mikroovn.explanation: "En mikroovn" means "a microwave". It is a shorter word for "en mikrobølgeovn" (a microwave oven). To say something is inside the microwave, use "i" (in): "Kaffen står i mikroovnen" (The coffee is in the microwave).

en mil.explanation: "En mil" means "a mil". It is an old Danish measure of distance of about 7.5 km, much longer than an English mile. A common phrase is "på mils afstand" (from miles away): "Det kan man se på mils afstand" (You can see that from miles away).

en milepæl.explanation: "En milepæl" means "a milestone". It is built from "mil" (an old measure of distance) and "en pæl" (a post). To say a project has reached an important point, use "at nå" (to reach): "Vi har nået en milepæl" (We have reached a milestone).

en milkshake.explanation: "En milkshake" means "a milkshake". It comes from the English word "milkshake". To order one, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en jordbærmilkshake" (I would like a strawberry milkshake).

en milliard.explanation: "En milliard" means "a billion". It is a thousand million: "en milliard kroner" (a billion kroner). Do not mix it up with "en billion", which is a million million, so a trillion: "en billion kroner" (a trillion kroner).

en mindehøjtidelighed.explanation: "En mindehøjtidelighed" means "a memorial service". It is built from "et minde" (a memory) and "en højtidelighed" (a ceremony). The same "minde" is in "en mindetale" (a memorial speech).

en mine.explanation: "En mine" means "a mine / a facial expression". When you talk about a place where coal or metal is dug out of the ground, it means "a mine": "en kulmine" (a coal mine). When you talk about a look on someone's face, it means "a facial expression": "en sur mine" (a sour look). Do not mix it up with "mine" (my): "mine børn" (my children).

en minister.explanation: "En minister" means "a minister". To say which area a minister leads, put the area first in one word: "en sundhedsminister" (a health minister).

en minoritet.explanation: "En minoritet" means "a minority". A common phrase is "en etnisk minoritet" (an ethnic minority).

en misforståelse.explanation: "En misforståelse" means "a misunderstanding". It is built from "mis-" and "en forståelse" (an understanding). The start "mis-" adds the idea of something going wrong, as in "mistillid" (distrust) and "mislykkes" (to fail).

en mission.explanation: "En mission" means "a mission". When you talk about a goal someone feels they must reach, you can also use "mission": "Hendes mission er at redde havet" (Her mission is to save the ocean).

en mistanke.explanation: "En mistanke" means "a suspicion". To say what you suspect, use "om" (about) after it: "Jeg har mistanke om, at han lyver" (I suspect that he is lying).

en mobil.explanation: "En mobil" means "a mobile phone". It is the short form of "en mobiltelefon" (a mobile phone). To say what you do on your phone, use "på" (on): "Jeg ser film på mobilen" (I watch films on my phone).

en mobiltelefon.explanation: "En mobiltelefon" means "a mobile phone". It is built from "mobil" (mobile) and "en telefon" (a phone). The short form is "en mobil": "Min mobil ligger på bordet" (My mobile phone is on the table).
